QUESTION: In Bulk Data Import for jobs, do I have to fill in the Job Code column?
JUDGING RULE: must contain ['optional', 'generated']; must NOT contain ['not covered', "isn't covered", 'not documented', 'does not cover', 'no information', 'must be filled', 'is rejected']; expected manual substring 'Bulk Data Import', pages None. CAPTURED MODEL INPUT (the excerpts exactly as sent):
[1] (Technical - Bulk Data Import (Operational) User Manual — 1.1.11.3 How To Download the Import Template)
* For the selected template click 'Download Template'.

* Fill in your data keeping the column headings unchanged — rows are read by their exact column names.

* Save the file as .csv, .xls or .xlsx (maximum 20 MB).

* Vessel Code must match the vessel selected on screen; rows with another vessel code are rejected.

* Component Code must already exist for the selected vessel; otherwise the row is rejected with 'Component Code does not exist for the selected vessel'.

* Jobs: the Job Code column is optional. A blank Job Code is accepted and a code is generated on import (JOB-XXXXXXX). Duplicate checking applies only to rows that supply a Job Code together with a Component Code for the vessel.

* Jobs: 'Assigned To' must be one of the recognised ranks and 'Approver' must be a rank from the Rank Master. The template's Master Data sheet lists the available ranks for reference.

---

[2] (Technical - Bulk Data Import (Operational) User Manual — TECHNICAL USER MANUAL — BULK DATA IMPORT (OPERATIONAL))
Revision: R3 (September 2026) / Audience: Office / Sail Admin

Bulk Data Import loads many records at once from a spreadsheet — Machinery Components, Jobs, Spares, Stores, Locations, Rotation Items and Work-Order History. The pattern is: download the template → fill it in → upload → the system validates the file (dry-run) → review the results → import → check the summary.

FULL ANSWER:
No. In Bulk Data Import for Jobs, the **Job Code** column may be left blank. The system generates a code on import in the format `JOB-XXXXXXX`.

If you provide a Job Code, duplicate checking applies only when the row also includes a Component Code for the selected vessel. **Assigned To** must be a recognised rank, and **Approver** must be a rank from the Rank Master.

Source: Bulk Data Import (Operational) User Manual, section 1.1.11.3 “How To Download the Import Template”.

CORRECTED CLAIMS — CASE 4
QUESTION: In work-order numbers, what do the vessel code and the segment after it mean, and what does an unplanned work order number look like?
JUDGING RULE: must contain ['vesselcode', 'uwo']; must NOT contain ['not covered', "isn't covered", 'not documented', 'does not cover', 'no information']; expected manual substring '(Operational)', pages None. Source note: R3 §1.1.14.1 and Ship-Side §1.1.13.2: <VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>; unplanned <VESSELCODE>-UWO-… (workOrderNumbering.ts:7-11).

  [4] Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — Introduction (p.28)

CAPTURED MODEL INPUT (the excerpts exactly as sent):
[1] (Technical - Ship-Side (Vessel Crew) Operational Notes — Preamble)
* Work-order numbers carry the vessel code as a prefix: planned work orders are \<VESSELCODE>-\<JOBCODE>-\<COMPONENTCODE>-\<YEAR>-\<NNN>, unplanned ones \<VESSELCODE>-UWO-\<COMPONENTCODE>-\<YEAR>-\<NNN>. Older work orders keep their original numbers; the running sequence continues across both formats.

---

[2] (Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes — 1.1.14.1 Work-Order Numbers Now Include the Vessel Code)
* New work orders are numbered with the vessel's code as a prefix: planned work orders `<VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>`, unplanned work orders `<VESSELCODE>-UWO-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>`.

* Existing work orders keep their original numbers; the running sequence continues across old and new formats, so numbering does not restart.

* If a vessel's code is not present on an instance, its new work orders use the older, non-prefixed format. The vessel code reaches a ship only through provisioning — the vessel master is not part of the routine sync — so a ship still producing old-format numbers needs its vessel code applied by re-provisioning or by support; the office 'Sync All' master refresh does not do this.

---

[3] (Technical - PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026 — Introduction (p.23))
* Work Orders (WO) is a structured instruction used onboard to plan, execute, and record maintenance activities for equipment and systems. It serves as the primary control mechanism to ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out systematically, safely, and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

---

[4] (Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — Introduction (p.28))
* Work Orders (WO) are a structured instruction used onboard to plan, execute, and record maintenance activities for equipment and systems. It serves as the primary control mechanism to ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out systematically, safely, and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

---

[5] (Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — 1.1.5.2 HOW TO CREATE AN UNPLANNED WORK ORDER (p.29))
* Go to the 'Work Orders' sub-sub module. (Ref Figure 43)

* Select the vessel from the 'Vessel' dropdown. (Ref Figure 43)

* Click on the '+ Unplanned W\.O' button to create an unplanned work order. (Ref Figure 43)

Screenshot of the Work Orders (W\.O) dashboard showing three steps: 1. Click here to access the 'Work Orders', 2. Click here to select a vessel, and 3. Click here to open an unplanned work order form.

Figure 43

* The 'Work Order Form – Unplanned Maintenance' form below appears after clicking the '+ Unplanned W\.O' button. (Ref Figure 44)

* Enter all required job details in Part A and click Save to store it as a draft. Then complete Part B and click Submit Work Order to generate the unplanned work order. (Ref Figure 44)

Screenshot of the Work Order Form - Unplanned showing the Save button highlighted with "Click the Save button to save it as a draft" and the Submit Work Order button highlighted with "After filling the form, click here to create an unplanned work order."

Figure 44

Page 29 of 64

FULL ANSWER:
- The **vessel code** is the prefix identifying the vessel.
- The segment immediately after it is:
  - **`JOBCODE`** for a planned work order.
  - **`UWO`** for an unplanned work order; it identifies the order as unplanned.

An unplanned work-order number looks like:

`<VESSELCODE>-UWO-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>`

The sequence continues across both old and new numbering formats and does not restart.

**Source:** Technical — Ship-Side Operational Notes, Preamble; Technical — Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours, §1.1.14.1.

[1] (Technical - Ship-Side (Vessel Crew) Operational Notes — Preamble)
* Work-order numbers carry the vessel code as a prefix: planned work orders are \<VESSELCODE>-\<JOBCODE>-\<COMPONENTCODE>-\<YEAR>-\<NNN>, unplanned ones \<VESSELCODE>-UWO-\<COMPONENTCODE>-\<YEAR>-\<NNN>. Older work orders keep their original numbers; the running sequence continues across both formats.

---

[2] (Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes — 1.1.14.1 Work-Order Numbers Now Include the Vessel Code)
* New work orders are numbered with the vessel's code as a prefix: planned work orders `<VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>`, unplanned work orders `<VESSELCODE>-UWO-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>`.

* Existing work orders keep their original numbers; the running sequence continues across old and new formats, so numbering does not restart.

* If a vessel's code is not present on an instance, its new work orders use the older, non-prefixed format. The vessel code reaches a ship only through provisioning — the vessel master is not part of the routine sync — so a ship still producing old-format numbers needs its vessel code applied by re-provisioning or by support; the office 'Sync All' master refresh does not do this.

---

[3] (Technical - PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026 — Introduction (p.23))

It serves as the primary control mechanism to ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out systematically, safely, and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

CAPTURED MODEL INPUT (the excerpts exactly as sent):
[1] (Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes — 1.1.14.6 Office Generation of Work Orders Is a Per-Vessel Switch)
* Only a Sail Admin can generate work orders directly from the office, and only for a vessel whose 'office work-order generation' switch is enabled (off by default). The switch is on the 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings' screen.

* With the switch off, the Sail Admin is told that office work-order generation is not enabled for the vessel and where to enable it. Other office roles are refused with a role message.

* Ships always generate their own work orders on their daily scan, regardless of this switch.

* The office 'Generate Now' button (Work Orders screen, with one vessel selected) runs an immediate, vessel-scoped generation instead of waiting for the daily sweep, subject to the same switch and role rule.

---

[2] (Technical - KB pilot: Office 'Generate Now' — generate a vessel's due work orders from the office.md — Office 'Generate Now' — generate a vessel's due work orders from the office)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 10 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Office
Who can do it (role): Sail Admin only. Any other office role is refused by the server with "Only a Sail Admin may generate work orders directly from the office."
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The selected vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch must be ON. It is OFF by default for every vessel; a Sail Admin enables it per vessel on the 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings' screen. With the switch off the server refuses with "Office work-order generation is not enabled for this vessel."
- One specific vessel must be selected on the Work Orders screen — the button is disabled for 'All' or 'My' vessels.
- Only jobs that are due and have no active work order are generated — the same rules as the ship's scan.
Steps:
1. Open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and select the vessel from the 'Vessel' dropdown.
2. Click 'Generate Now' in the toolbar of the Work Orders screen (next to 'Planner' and 'Export').
3. The server runs the generation sweep for that vessel only and returns; the new work orders appear under the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- The button is shown to Sail Admin, Client Admin and Head of Dept on the office instance, but the server accepts Sail Admin only; the other two roles see a button whose every click is refused. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md (existing standalone note).
- On a ship instance this gate always allows generation (the ship's own scan is the normal path).
- 'Generate Now' does NOT apply to the per-job 'Generate WO' button on the Components page, which has its own, different condition — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not mention 'Generate Now', the Sail Admin restriction or the per-vessel switch. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

---

[3] (Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

---

[4] (Technical - KB pilot: Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan.md — Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 6 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Vessel
Who can do it (role): None — no user action. Planned (scheduled) work orders are created by the ship system itself.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The instance must be a ship instance; the scan does not run on the office (shore) instance.
- The job must be active and attached to a component, with a frequency and a next due date (the job schedule shown in Components → Part C).
- The job must not already have an active work order — one active work order per job at a time.
Steps:
1. Nothing to do. The ship system runs the job-due scan once every 24 hours by default (interval configurable through JOB_DUE_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS) and creates a work order for every job that is due.
2. To see the result, open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and use the status tabs: Scheduled (jobs planned with a future due date), Due (due within the current period), Overdue (past due date, not completed).
3. The work-order number is prefixed with the vessel code: <VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- If a job already has an active work order, the scan does not create another one for it.
- A work order can be generated ahead of the scan for one job with 'Generate WO' on the Components page — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
- On the office instance no scan runs. Office-side generation is done by a user in one of two ways: 'Generate Now' for a whole vessel (Sail Admin AND the vessel switch) — see office-generate-now.md — or per-job 'Generate WO' from Components (the vessel switch) — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not describe automatic generation at all. They describe the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs and the job frequency / next due date but never say that the system creates the work orders. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

---

[5] (Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — Introduction (p.28))
* Work Orders (WO) are a structured instruction used onboard to plan, execute, and record maintenance activities for equipment and systems. It serves as the primary control mechanism to ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out systematically, safely, and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

FULL ANSWER:
From the office, only a **Sail Admin** can generate work orders, and only for a vessel with the **“office work-order generation” switch enabled** on **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**.

1. Select one vessel on the **Work Orders** screen.
2. Click **Generate Now**.
3. If the switch is **off**, generation is refused with a message that office work-order generation is not enabled for that vessel. Other office roles are also refused because they are not Sail Admins.

The switch is **off by default**. Ships generate their own work orders through their daily scan regardless of this office switch.

The June published manual excerpt does not specify this office role or switch behavior; these details come from the operational update and draft code-derived guidance.

**Source:** [1] *Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes*, §1.1.14.6; [2] *KB pilot: Office “Generate Now” — generate a vessel’s due work orders from the office*.

   1. A **Sail Admin only** may select one vessel on the Work Orders screen and click **Generate Now**.
   2. The vessel’s **office work-order generation** switch must be enabled on **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**. It is off by default.
   3. If the switch is off, generation is refused with: **“Office work-order generation is not enabled for this vessel.”** Other office roles are refused because only a Sail Admin may use this function.
   4. The sweep creates only due jobs without an active work order.

2. **Per-job “Generate WO”**
   1. From **Components**, select the vessel in the office, open the component, go to **Part C**, and click **Generate WO**.
   2. Choose **Planning**, **Breakdown**, or **Other**.
   3. There is **no role check**, but normal sign-in and vessel access apply. In the office, the vessel switch must be on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order.
   4. If the switch is off, this office generation path cannot be used.

3. **Unplanned work order**
   1. From **Work Orders**, select the vessel in the office and click **+ Unplanned W.O**.
   2. Complete **Part A**, save, complete **Part B**, and submit the work order.
   3. No special role check or office-generation switch is required; normal sign-in and vessel access apply.

The first two procedures are draft code-derived guidance, while the published operational update specifically confirms that direct office generation requires a Sail Admin and an enabled vessel switch.

**Source:**
- Generate Now: *Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes*, §1.1.14.6; draft *Office “Generate Now” — generate a vessel’s due work orders from the office*, §Office “Generate Now”.
- Per-job “Generate WO”: draft *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, §How work orders are created.
- Unplanned work order: draft *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, §How work orders are created.

[1] (Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes — 1.1.14.6 Office Generation of Work Orders Is a Per-Vessel Switch)
* Only a Sail Admin can generate work orders directly from the office, and only for a vessel whose 'office work-order generation' switch is enabled (off by default). The switch is on the 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings' screen.

* With the switch off, the Sail Admin is told that office work-order generation is not enabled for the vessel and where to enable it. Other office roles are refused with a role message.

* Ships always generate their own work orders on their daily scan, regardless of this switch.

* The office 'Generate Now' button (Work Orders screen, with one vessel selected) runs an immediate, vessel-scoped generation instead of waiting for the daily sweep, subject to the same switch and role rule.

[2] (Technical - KB pilot: Office 'Generate Now' — generate a vessel's due work orders from the office.md — Office 'Generate Now' — generate a vessel's due work orders from the office)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 10 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Office
Who can do it (role): Sail Admin only. Any other office role is refused by the server with "Only a Sail Admin may generate work orders directly from the office."
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The selected vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch must be ON. It is OFF by default for every vessel; a Sail Admin enables it per vessel on the 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings' screen. With the switch off the server refuses with "Office work-order generation is not enabled for this vessel."
- One specific vessel must be selected on the Work Orders screen — the button is disabled for 'All' or 'My' vessels.
- Only jobs that are due and have no active work order are generated — the same rules as the ship's scan.
Steps:
1. Open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and select the vessel from the 'Vessel' dropdown.
2. Click 'Generate Now' in the toolbar of the Work Orders screen (next to 'Planner' and 'Export').
3. The server runs the generation sweep for that vessel only and returns; the new work orders appear under the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- The button is shown to Sail Admin, Client Admin and Head of Dept on the office instance, but the server accepts Sail Admin only; the other two roles see a button whose every click is refused. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md (existing standalone note).
- On a ship instance this gate always allows generation (the ship's own scan is the normal path).
- 'Generate Now' does NOT apply to the per-job 'Generate WO' button on the Components page, which has its own, different condition — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not mention 'Generate Now', the Sail Admin restriction or the per-vessel switch. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

[3] (Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

[4] (Technical - KB pilot: Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan.md — Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 6 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Vessel
Who can do it (role): None — no user action. Planned (scheduled) work orders are created by the ship system itself.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The instance must be a ship instance; the scan does not run on the office (shore) instance.
- The job must be active and attached to a component, with a frequency and a next due date (the job schedule shown in Components → Part C).
- The job must not already have an active work order — one active work order per job at a time.
Steps:
1. Nothing to do. The ship system runs the job-due scan once every 24 hours by default (interval configurable through JOB_DUE_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS) and creates a work order for every job that is due.
2. To see the result, open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and use the status tabs: Scheduled (jobs planned with a future due date), Due (due within the current period), Overdue (past due date, not completed).
3. The work-order number is prefixed with the vessel code: <VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- If a job already has an active work order, the scan does not create another one for it.
- A work order can be generated ahead of the scan for one job with 'Generate WO' on the Components page — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
- On the office instance no scan runs. Office-side generation is done by a user in one of two ways: 'Generate Now' for a whole vessel (Sail Admin AND the vessel switch) — see office-generate-now.md — or per-job 'Generate WO' from Components (the vessel switch) — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not describe automatic generation at all. They describe the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs and the job frequency / next due date but never say that the system creates the work orders. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

---

[5] (Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — Introduction (p.28))
* Work Orders (WO) are a structured instruction used onboard to plan, execute, and record maintenance activities for equipment and systems. It serves as the primary control mechanism to ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out systematically, safely, and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

FULL ANSWER:
From the office, the supported ways are:

1. **Generate Now for a whole vessel**
   1. Only a **Sail Admin** can do this.
   2. The selected vessel’s **office work-order generation** switch must be **ON**. It is OFF by default and is enabled on **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**.
   3. Select one vessel on the **Work Orders** screen and click **Generate Now**.
   4. If the switch is OFF, generation is refused with a message that office generation is not enabled for that vessel. Other office roles are refused because only a Sail Admin may generate directly from the office.

2. **Per-job “Generate WO”**
   1. No special role is required; normal sign-in and vessel access still apply.
   2. In the office, the vessel’s office work-order generation switch must be **ON**.
   3. The job must be active and must not already have an active work order.
   4. If the switch is OFF, this office action is not available under its stated prerequisites.

3. **Unplanned work order**
   1. No special role or office-generation switch is required; normal sign-in and vessel access apply.
   2. Create it through **Work Orders → + Unplanned W.O → Part A → Save → Part B → Submit Work Order**.

The ship’s automatic daily generation is separate: ships generate their own planned work orders regardless of the office-generation switch. The role and switch details above are from draft code-derived guidance, while the recent operational update also confirms the Sail Admin and switch rules for office generation.

**Source:**  
- **Generate Now:** *Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes*, §1.1.14.6; draft *Office “Generate Now” — generate a vessel’s due work orders from the office*.  
- **Per-job “Generate WO”:** draft *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*.  
- **Unplanned work order:** draft *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*.

2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

[4] (Technical - KB pilot: Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan.md — Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 6 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Vessel
Who can do it (role): None — no user action. Planned (scheduled) work orders are created by the ship system itself.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The instance must be a ship instance; the scan does not run on the office (shore) instance.
- The job must be active and attached to a component, with a frequency and a next due date (the job schedule shown in Components → Part C).
- The job must not already have an active work order — one active work order per job at a time.
Steps:
1. Nothing to do. The ship system runs the job-due scan once every 24 hours by default (interval configurable through JOB_DUE_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS) and creates a work order for every job that is due.
2. To see the result, open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and use the status tabs: Scheduled (jobs planned with a future due date), Due (due within the current period), Overdue (past due date, not completed).
3. The work-order number is prefixed with the vessel code: <VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- If a job already has an active work order, the scan does not create another one for it.
- A work order can be generated ahead of the scan for one job with 'Generate WO' on the Components page — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
- On the office instance no scan runs. Office-side generation is done by a user in one of two ways: 'Generate Now' for a whole vessel (Sail Admin AND the vessel switch) — see office-generate-now.md — or per-job 'Generate WO' from Components (the vessel switch) — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not describe automatic generation at all. They describe the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs and the job frequency / next due date but never say that the system creates the work orders. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

---

[5] (Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — Introduction (p.28))
* Work Orders (WO) are a structured instruction used onboard to plan, execute, and record maintenance activities for equipment and systems. It serves as the primary control mechanism to ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out systematically, safely, and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

FULL ANSWER:
The supported office ways are:

1. **Generate Now for a whole vessel**
   1. Only a **Sail Admin** can use it.
   2. A single vessel must be selected on the **Work Orders** screen.
   3. The vessel’s **office work-order generation** switch must be **ON**. It is off by default and is enabled on **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**.
   4. If the switch is off, generation is refused with a message that office work-order generation is not enabled for that vessel. Other office roles are refused because only a Sail Admin may generate directly from the office.

2. **Per-job “Generate WO” from Components**
   1. There is **no role check** for this action; normal sign-in and vessel access still apply.
   2. In the office, the vessel’s office work-order generation switch must be **ON**.
   3. If the switch is off, this office generation path cannot be used. The excerpts do not specify its refusal message.

3. **Unplanned work order**
   1. There is **no role check** and **no office-generation switch requirement**.
   2. Create it through **Work Orders → + Unplanned W.O → Part A → Save → Part B → Submit Work Order**.

Ships generate planned work orders through their daily scan; this is not automatic office generation.

**Source:**  
- Generate Now: *Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes*, §1.1.14.6; draft KB guidance, *Office “Generate Now”*, §Office “Generate Now”.  
- Per-job “Generate WO”: draft KB guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, §How work orders are created.  
- Unplanned work: draft KB guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, §How work orders are created.

[1] (Technical - Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes — 1.1.14.6 Office Generation of Work Orders Is a Per-Vessel Switch)
* Only a Sail Admin can generate work orders directly from the office, and only for a vessel whose 'office work-order generation' switch is enabled (off by default). The switch is on the 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings' screen.

* With the switch off, the Sail Admin is told that office work-order generation is not enabled for the vessel and where to enable it. Other office roles are refused with a role message.

* Ships always generate their own work orders on their daily scan, regardless of this switch.

* The office 'Generate Now' button (Work Orders screen, with one vessel selected) runs an immediate, vessel-scoped generation instead of waiting for the daily sweep, subject to the same switch and role rule.

[2] (Technical - KB pilot: Office 'Generate Now' — generate a vessel's due work orders from the office.md — Office 'Generate Now' — generate a vessel's due work orders from the office)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 10 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Office
Who can do it (role): Sail Admin only. Any other office role is refused by the server with "Only a Sail Admin may generate work orders directly from the office."
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The selected vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch must be ON. It is OFF by default for every vessel; a Sail Admin enables it per vessel on the 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings' screen. With the switch off the server refuses with "Office work-order generation is not enabled for this vessel."
- One specific vessel must be selected on the Work Orders screen — the button is disabled for 'All' or 'My' vessels.
- Only jobs that are due and have no active work order are generated — the same rules as the ship's scan.
Steps:
1. Open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and select the vessel from the 'Vessel' dropdown.
2. Click 'Generate Now' in the toolbar of the Work Orders screen (next to 'Planner' and 'Export').
3. The server runs the generation sweep for that vessel only and returns; the new work orders appear under the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- The button is shown to Sail Admin, Client Admin and Head of Dept on the office instance, but the server accepts Sail Admin only; the other two roles see a button whose every click is refused. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md (existing standalone note).
- On a ship instance this gate always allows generation (the ship's own scan is the normal path).
- 'Generate Now' does NOT apply to the per-job 'Generate WO' button on the Components page, which has its own, different condition — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not mention 'Generate Now', the Sail Admin restriction or the per-vessel switch. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.

* The office 'Generate Now' button (Work Orders screen, with one vessel selected) runs an immediate, vessel-scoped generation instead of waiting for the daily sweep, subject to the same switch and role rule.

[3] (Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.

[4] (Technical - KB pilot: Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan.md — Planned work orders — generated automatically by the ship's daily job-due scan)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 6 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Vessel
Who can do it (role): None — no user action. Planned (scheduled) work orders are created by the ship system itself.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):
- The instance must be a ship instance; the scan does not run on the office (shore) instance.
- The job must be active and attached to a component, with a frequency and a next due date (the job schedule shown in Components → Part C).
- The job must not already have an active work order — one active work order per job at a time.
Steps:
1. Nothing to do. The ship system runs the job-due scan once every 24 hours by default (interval configurable through JOB_DUE_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS) and creates a work order for every job that is due.
2. To see the result, open the 'Work Orders' sub-sub-module and use the status tabs: Scheduled (jobs planned with a future due date), Due (due within the current period), Overdue (past due date, not completed).
3. The work-order number is prefixed with the vessel code: <VESSELCODE>-<JOBCODE>-<COMPONENTCODE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>.
Exceptions / edge cases:
- If a job already has an active work order, the scan does not create another one for it.
- A work order can be generated ahead of the scan for one job with 'Generate WO' on the Components page — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
- On the office instance no scan runs. Office-side generation is done by a user in one of two ways: 'Generate Now' for a whole vessel (Sail Admin AND the vessel switch) — see office-generate-now.md — or per-job 'Generate WO' from Components (the vessel switch) — see office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
Where the manual differs:
- The June manuals do not describe automatic generation at all. They describe the Scheduled / Due / Overdue tabs and the job frequency / next due date but never say that the system creates the work orders. Recorded in CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

[5] (Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — Introduction (p.28))
* Work Orders (WO) are a structured instruction used onboard to plan, execute, and record maintenance activities for equipment and systems. It serves as the primary control mechanism to ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out systematically, safely, and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

FULL ANSWER:
Only a **Sail Admin** can generate work orders directly from the office, and only for a vessel whose **“office work-order generation”** switch is enabled on the **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings** screen. The switch is off by default.

1. Select one vessel on the office **Work Orders** screen.
2. Click **Generate Now**.
3. If the switch is off, generation is refused with a message that office work-order generation is not enabled for that vessel, along with where to enable it.
4. If another office role attempts it, generation is refused with a role message: **“Only a Sail Admin may generate work orders directly from the office.”**

Ships generate their own work orders through their daily scan regardless of this office switch.

**Source:**  
- Technical — *Recent Updates & Changed Behaviours (Operational) Notes*, §1.1.14.6.  
- Draft code-derived guidance — *Office “Generate Now” — generate a vessel’s due work orders from the office*, §Office “Generate Now”.

[5] (Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026 — Introduction (p.28))
* Work Orders (WO) are a structured instruction used onboard to plan, execute, and record maintenance activities for equipment and systems. It serves as the primary control mechanism to ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out systematically, safely, and in compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

FULL ANSWER:
The excerpts support three office ways to create work orders:

1. **Generate Now for a vessel**
   - Only a **Sail Admin** can do this.
   - Select **one vessel** on the **Work Orders** screen and click **Generate Now**.
   - The vessel’s **office work-order generation** switch must be **ON**. It is OFF by default and is enabled on **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**.
   - If the switch is OFF, the server refuses the request with: **“Office work-order generation is not enabled for this vessel.”**
   - Other office roles are refused with: **“Only a Sail Admin may generate work orders directly from the office.”**

2. **Generate WO for one job**
   - Go to **Components**, select the vessel in the office, open the component, choose **Part C → Generate WO**, and select the reason.
   - There is **no role check**, but normal sign-in and vessel access apply.
   - The vessel’s office work-order generation switch must be **ON**; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order.

3. **Create an unplanned work order**
   - Go to **Work Orders → + Unplanned W.O**, complete **Part A**, save, then complete **Part B** and submit.
   - No special role check or office-generation switch is required; normal sign-in and vessel access apply.

The published June manual excerpt does not state these office role and switch rules; they come from the draft, code-derived guidance.

* Use the office screens for the assigned vessels, and switch between 'Me' (own work) and 'My Team' (team's work) on the PMS Dashboard.

[2] (Technical - Roles & Permissions (Operational) User Manual — 1.1.12.5 What a Superintendent (Office) User Can Do)
* View and manage maintenance for assigned vessels (use the 'My Vessel' scope to focus on them).

* Review dashboards, work orders, running hours, spares, stores, defects, certificates and surveys.

* Review postponement requests and approve / reject work as permitted by the approval configuration.

* Reopen a completed work order or reject a completion back to the vessel with remarks (available to the Office, PMS Admin and Sail Admin roles), and follow the selected vessel's activity on the Superintendent page (pending / acknowledged / information tabs).

FULL ANSWER:
No. The documentation does not say that a Head of Department can do everything an office user can do.

A Head of Department can:

1. Use the office screens for assigned vessels.
2. Switch the PMS Dashboard between **Me** (own work) and **My Team** (team work).
3. Not approve postponement requests when no approval steps are configured; that approval is reserved for office roles.

The Office Superintendent role additionally supports:

1. Managing maintenance for assigned vessels using **My Vessel**.
2. Reviewing dashboards, work orders, running hours, spares, stores, defects, certificates and surveys.
3. Reviewing and approving or rejecting postponement requests as allowed by the approval configuration.
4. Reopening completed work orders or rejecting completion back to the vessel with remarks; this is available to Office, PMS Admin and Sail Admin roles.
5. Exporting records from screens that provide an **Export** button.

The excerpts do not confirm that a Head of Department has these additional office-user permissions.

- Head of Department capabilities — *Roles & Permissions (Operational) User Manual*, §1.1.12.6.

[5] (Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

FULL ANSWER:
No—**on the ship, planned work orders are created automatically by the PMS**. The system scans once daily and generates them from each job’s frequency and next due date; no user action is required.

**In the office**, planned work orders are not generated automatically. A **Sail Admin** must:

1. Open the Work Orders screen for the vessel.
2. Click **Generate Now**.

The vessel’s **office work-order generation switch must be ON**. Normal sign-in and vessel access also apply.

The draft code-derived guidance also supports two other creation paths: generating a work order for one job through **Components → Part C → Generate WO**, or creating an **unplanned work order** through **Work Orders → + Unplanned W.O**.

**Source:**
- Planned work orders — *KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, “How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order” (draft code-derived guidance, repository revision cf5241ad).
- One-job work orders — same guidance, step 2.
- Unplanned work orders — *Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026*, §1.1.5.2, p.29; *Technical - PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026*, §1.1.5.2, p.24.

Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

FULL ANSWER:
No—planned work orders do not always require you to create them yourself. The draft code-derived guidance supports these planned-work-order paths:

1. **Automatic ship generation:** On the ship, PMS creates scheduled work orders automatically once a day from each job’s frequency and next due date. No user action is required.

2. **Office “Generate Now”:** In the office, automatic generation does not run by itself. A **Sail Admin** can select one vessel on the Work Orders screen and click **Generate Now**, but only when that vessel’s **office work-order generation** switch is ON. The switch is set in **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings** and is off by default. A job with an active work order cannot receive another one.

3. **Per-job “Generate WO”:** Open **Components**; in the office, select the vessel; open the component, go to **Part C**, click **Generate WO**, and choose **Planning**, **Breakdown**, or **Other**. No special role check applies, but normal sign-in and vessel access are required. In the office, the vessel switch must be ON; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order.

The published June manuals describe per-job/unplanned creation and work-order planning, but do not describe automatic planned generation or **Generate Now**. The additional details above come from draft, code-derived guidance inspected at revision **cf5241ad**.

**Source:**
- Automatic ship generation — draft code-derived guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, planned work orders.
- Office “Generate Now” — draft code-derived guidance, same section; related `office-generate-now.md`.
- Per-job “Generate WO” — draft code-derived guidance, same section; related `office-generate-wo-per-job.md`.

FULL ANSWER:

FULL ANSWER:
You do **not always have to create planned work orders yourself**. The supported ways are:

1. **Automatic scheduled creation on the ship**
   - The ship system creates work orders automatically once a day from each job’s frequency and next due date.
   - No user action is required.

2. **Office “Generate Now”**
   - A **Sail Admin** can open the Work Orders screen and click **Generate Now** for one vessel.

   - The job must be active and must not already have an active work order.

The automatic-generation and role/switch details come from the **draft, code-derived guidance**, not the published manuals. The published excerpts provided describe unplanned and pre-planned work orders, but do not describe how scheduled planned work orders are automatically generated.

[5] (Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

FULL ANSWER:
No—not always. The draft guidance supports these planned-work-order paths:

1. **Automatic ship generation**
   - On the ship, PMS creates scheduled work orders automatically once per day from each job’s frequency and next due date.
   - No user action is required.

2. **Office “Generate Now”**
   - In the Office, nothing runs automatically.
   - A **Sail Admin** can click **Generate Now** on the Work Orders screen for one vessel.
   - The vessel’s **office work-order generation switch must be ON**; it is off by default and is set in **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**.

3. **Generate a work order for one job**
   - Go to **Components**; in the Office, select the vessel.
   - Open the component, go to **Part C**, click **Generate WO**, and choose **Planning**, **Breakdown**, or **Other**.
   - There is no role check for this path, but normal sign-in and vessel access apply. In the Office, the vessel switch must be ON.
   - The job must be active and must not already have an active work order.

The published June manuals describe unplanned work orders and pre-planning, but do not describe automatic ship generation or Office **Generate Now**. The automatic-generation and role/switch details come from draft, code-derived guidance marked as not a published manual.

**Source:**  
- Planned automatic generation: *KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, “Planned (scheduled) work orders.”  
- Office **Generate Now**: same guidance, “Planned (scheduled) work orders” and prerequisites.  
- Per-job **Generate WO**: same guidance, “One job on demand.”  
- Published manual comparison: *PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin*, §§1.1.5.2–1.1.5.3; *PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific*, §§1.1.5.2–1.1.5.3.

FULL ANSWER:
Planned work orders do not normally require you to create them manually:

1. **On the ship:** PMS automatically creates planned work orders once a day from each job’s frequency and next due date. No user action is required.

2. **In the office:** PMS does not generate them automatically. A **Sail Admin** can select a vessel and click **Generate Now** on the Work Orders screen, provided the vessel’s **office work-order generation** switch is ON. The switch is set in **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings** and is OFF by default.

The automatic ship generation and office **Generate Now** process are described in draft, code-derived guidance rather than the published June manuals. Those manuals describe unplanned and per-job work-order creation, but not planned-work-order generation.

**Source:** Draft code-derived guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, items 1 and “Prerequisites”; related procedures *planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md* and *office-generate-now.md*.

FULL ANSWER:
Planned work orders are created in two ways:

1. **On the ship:** You do not create them yourself. The ship system automatically generates them once a day from each job’s frequency and next due date. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply, and a job with an active work order cannot receive another one.

2. **In the office:** A **Sail Admin** can manually click **Generate Now** on the Work Orders screen for one vessel. The vessel’s **office work-order generation** switch must be ON; it is set in **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**. The office does not generate planned work orders automatically.

The June published manuals do not describe automatic ship generation or the office **Generate Now** function; these details come from draft, code-derived guidance based on application revision `cf5241ad`, which the application owner confirmed is running in the Technical application.

[5] (Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

FULL ANSWER:
Planned work orders are created in two ways:

1. **On the ship:** The PMS creates them automatically once a day from each job’s frequency and next due date. You do not create them manually. The job must not already have an active work order.

2. **In the Office:** Nothing runs automatically. A **Sail Admin** can:
   1. Open the **Work Orders** screen.
   2. Select one vessel.
   3. Click **Generate Now**.

   This requires the vessel’s **office work-order generation** switch to be ON. The switch is OFF by default and is set in **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**. Normal sign-in and vessel access also apply. A job with an active work order cannot receive another one.

The June published manuals describe per-job and unplanned work-order creation, but do not document planned automatic generation or the Office **Generate Now** process. Those details come from the draft, code-derived guidance.

**Source:** Draft code-derived guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, planned work orders section; published June PMS manuals, sections 1.1.5.2–1.1.5.3, which document other work-order procedures.

FULL ANSWER:
The excerpts support three ways to create a work order. The three-way overview and its role/switch conditions are from draft, code-derived guidance at revision `cf5241ad`.

1. **Planned work order — automatic generation**
   - On the **ship**, the system generates planned work orders automatically once a day from each job’s frequency and next due date; no user action is required.
   - In the **Office**, nothing runs automatically. A **Sail Admin** can use **Generate Now** for one vessel, but only when that vessel’s **office work-order generation switch is ON**.

2. **Generate a work order for one job on demand**
   1. Go to **Components**.
   2. In the **Office**, select the vessel.
   3. Open the component and go to **Part C**.
   4. Click **Generate WO**.
   5. Select the reason: **Planning**, **Breakdown**, or **Other**.
   
   No special role check is stated; normal sign-in and vessel access apply. In the Office, the vessel’s office work-order generation switch must be **ON**. The job must be active and must not already have an active work order.

3. **Create an unplanned work order**
   1. Go to the **Work Orders** sub-sub-module.
   2. In the **Office**, select the vessel from the **Vessel** dropdown. On the ship, the vessel is fixed, so this step does not apply.
   3. Click **+ Unplanned W.O**.
   4. Enter the required job details in **Part A**, then click **Save** to store the form as a draft.
   5. Complete **Part B** and click **Submit Work Order** to create the work order.
   
   No special role check or switch is required; normal sign-in and vessel access apply. The published Office manual also requires selecting the vessel, while the Vessel manual omits that step because the ship instance is single-vessel.

**Source:**
- Planned automatic generation and Office **Generate Now**: draft code-derived guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, section “How work orders are created.”
- Per-job **Generate WO**: draft code-derived guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, section “How work orders are created.”
- Unplanned work order: *PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026*, §1.1.5.2, p. 29; *PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026*, §1.1.5.2, p. 24; draft guidance, *Create an unplanned work order ('+ Unplanned W.O')*.

Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 14 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 4 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): No role or switch check was found on this path; normal authentication and vessel access still apply (the user must be signed in and able to open the Work Orders page for that vessel).
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state):

- On the office instance a vessel must be selected from the 'Vessel' dropdown first.
Steps:

- None recorded in this pilot. (An open question about running-hours readings on the unplanned form's Part B is logged in REVIEW.md, not stated here.)

- None found for the steps themselves. The Vessel manual has no 'select vessel' step (ship instance is single-vessel).

[5] (Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order.md — How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order)
Provenance note: draft code-derived guidance, not a published manual. 3 statement(s) come from the June PMS manuals; 7 statement(s) about roles, switches and automatic generation were inspected in the Technical application code at repository revision cf5241ad6, which the application owner has confirmed is the code running in the Technical application. Where this guidance and a manual differ, say which source says what.
Applies to: Both
Who can do it (role): Depends on the way — (1) planned: nobody, the ship system creates them; office 'Generate Now': Sail Admin only; (2) per-job 'Generate WO': no role check; (3) unplanned: no role check. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply to all.
Prerequisites (switches, settings, job/component state): Office 'Generate Now' and office per-job 'Generate WO' both need the vessel's 'office work-order generation' switch ON (off by default, set by a Sail Admin on 'Lead Time & Grace Period Settings'). Unplanned needs no switch. A job with an active work order cannot get another one.
Steps:
1. Planned (scheduled) work orders — generated by the system from each job's frequency and next due date. ON THE SHIP: automatic, once a day, no user action. IN THE OFFICE: nothing runs automatically; a Sail Admin can click 'Generate Now' on the Work Orders screen for one vessel, only if that vessel's switch is on. Details: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md and office-generate-now.md.
2. One job on demand — Components → (Office: select the vessel) → open the component → Part C → 'Generate WO' → choose the reason (Planning / Breakdown / Other). No role check on this path (sign-in and vessel access still apply); in the office only if the vessel switch is on; the job must be active and must not already have an active work order. Details: office-generate-wo-per-job.md.
3. Unplanned work — Work Orders → (Office: select the vessel) → '+ Unplanned W.O' → Part A, Save → Part B, Submit Work Order. No role check on this path, no switch. Details: unplanned-wo.md.
Exceptions / edge cases: The Sail Admin requirement belongs to 'Generate Now' only; it does not apply to per-job 'Generate WO' or to unplanned work orders.
Where the manual differs: The June manuals describe only ways 2 and 3 and state no office conditions; automatic ship generation and 'Generate Now' are absent from them. See CONFLICTS.md.
Related procedures: planned-wo-ship-daily-scan.md · office-generate-now.md · office-generate-wo-per-job.md · unplanned-wo.md

FULL ANSWER:
The excerpts support these ways to create a new work order:

1. **Planned work order — automatic on the ship**
   1. The ship system generates work orders automatically once a day from each job’s frequency and next due date.
   2. No user action is required.
   3. Normal sign-in and vessel access apply.

2. **Planned work order — Office “Generate Now”**
   1. Open the **Work Orders** screen and select a vessel.
   2. Click **Generate Now**.
   3. This is available only to a **Sail Admin** and only when that vessel’s **office work-order generation switch** is ON. The switch is set in **Lead Time & Grace Period Settings**.
   4. The office system does not generate these automatically.

3. **Generate a work order for one job on demand**
   1. Open **Components**.
   2. In the Office, select the vessel.
   3. Open the component and go to **Part C**.
   4. Click **Generate WO**.
   5. Select the reason: **Planning**, **Breakdown**, or **Other**.
   6. The job must be active and must not already have an active work order.
   7. In the Office, the vessel’s **office work-order generation switch** must be ON. No special role is required; normal sign-in and vessel access apply.

4. **Create an unplanned work order**
   1. Go to the **Work Orders** sub-sub-module.
   2. In the Office, select the vessel from the **Vessel** dropdown. On the ship, the vessel is fixed and this step does not apply.
   3. Click **+ Unplanned W.O**.
   4. Enter the required job details in **Part A** and click **Save** to store the form as a draft.
   5. Complete **Part B** and click **Submit Work Order** to create the work order.
   6. No role check or vessel-generation switch is required; normal sign-in and vessel access apply.

The automatic-generation and Office **Generate Now** procedures come from draft, code-derived guidance and are not described in the supplied published manual excerpts. The published manuals supplied here document the unplanned-work-order procedure.

**Source:**  
- Planned ship generation and Office **Generate Now**: *Technical - KB pilot: How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, “How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order” (draft code-derived guidance, repository revision cf5241ad).  
- Per-job **Generate WO**: same draft guidance and section.  
- Unplanned work order: *PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026*, §1.1.5.2, p.29; *PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific_R3_08.07.2026*, §1.1.5.2, p.24; and the draft *Create an unplanned work order ('+ Unplanned W.O')* guidance.

   - In **Components**, select the vessel in the Office, if applicable.
   - Open the component and go to **Part C**.
   - Click **Generate WO**.
   - Select the reason: **Planning**, **Breakdown**, or **Other**.
   - In the Office, the vessel’s **office work-order generation switch must be ON**.
   - The job must be active and must not already have an active work order. There is no role check stated for this action.

3. **Create an unplanned work order**
   - **Office:** go to **Work Orders** and select the vessel from the **Vessel** dropdown. On the ship, the vessel is fixed, so no vessel selection is required.
   - Click **+ Unplanned W.O**.
   - Enter the required job details in **Part A** and click **Save** to store the form as a draft.
   - Complete **Part B** and click **Submit Work Order** to create the work order.
   - No role check or vessel work-order-generation switch is stated for this path; normal sign-in and vessel access still apply.

The planned-generation and role/switch details come from draft code-derived guidance, marked as not a published manual. The June manuals describe the per-job and unplanned approaches but do not include the automatic ship generation or Office **Generate Now** process.

**Source:**
- Planned automatic generation: draft code-derived guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, item 1.
- One-job generation: draft code-derived guidance, *How work orders are created — the three ways to create a work order*, item 2.
- Unplanned work order: *PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin*, §1.1.5.2, p.29; *PMS User Manual_Vessel Specific*, §1.1.5.2, p.24; draft code-derived guidance, *Create an unplanned work order*.
